## Two new things to detect, one new thing to be scared of

Turns out Tile trackers and Ring doorbells were already being detected this whole time — just filed under the wrong names. Tile was getting lumped in with AirTag ("eh, it's a tracker, close enough") and Ring was getting lumped in with generic CAMERA ("eh, it's a camera, close enough"). Neither of those was actually enough anymore, so both got promoted to real, dedicated detection types with their own colors, their own icons, and their own line in the counter row. Bureaucracy, but for surveillance gear.

Also: the FIRE background now has a spooky night sky behind it — twinkling stars, a pale unsettling moon, and a gnarled dead tree that occasionally gets swallowed by a tall flame like it's part of the scene, because it is. Flames reach higher now too. The snowman on the SNOWFALL background got bigger, because the old one looked malnourished. And "!! DETECTION !!" no longer awkwardly overlaps its own border, which is the kind of bug that's been staring at everyone for a while and nobody said anything.

The flasher also has a proper favicon now instead of a boring default browser icon, because that mattered to me more than it probably should have.

### The actually-useful part
- **Added `TILE`** as its own detection type — Tile's two Bluetooth SIG-assigned service UUIDs (`0xFEED`, `0xFEEC`), previously misclassified as AirTag
- **Added `RING`** as its own detection type — Ring LLC's full 15-prefix registered WiFi OUI block, previously misclassified as generic camera
- Web flasher's detection legend and the FAQ updated to match (thirteen types now, not eleven)
- Web flasher has a Squachy favicon
- FIRE background: taller flame reach, twinkling stars, a pale moon, and a gnarled tree silhouette — all gated so they never draw through actual flame/smoke
- SNOWFALL's easter-egg snowman scaled up ~1.4x
- Fixed: ALERT screen's "!! DETECTION !!" overlapping the pulsing red border
